purpose: Five DOJ Immigrant and Employee Rights Section resolution summaries represented as separate case-level remedy events; agency-reported payments and offers are kept distinct from worker-confirmed receipt, restored opportunity, and later action.

events.geography: United States; named charging-party employment resolution, employer identity not disclosed in retained summary
events.date_precision: IER resolution date; summary updated September 15, 2026
events.denominator: One named charging-party resolution; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary
events.missingness: No claimant identifier, payment instrument/date, employer name, alternative job, continued employment, household outcome, trust, action, or exit is retained
events.exposure: A naturalized US citizen alleged that a staffing company withdrew a position after requesting citizenship proof
events.alternatives_before_action: Other jobs, non-use, appeal choices, and the charging party's feasible alternatives are not reported
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The summary reports $5,600 in back pay received by the charging party; the underlying lost opportunity and net household effect are not disclosed
events.choice_or_response: The charging party pursued an IER resolution; the public summary does not describe effort, timing, or any accepted employment alternative
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controlled the disputed hiring decision; IER controlled the investigation/resolution route, but the full decision chain is not disclosed
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Agency-reported back-pay payment and relevant staff training on the anti-discrimination provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act
events.remedy_receipt: Agency summary reports payment; payment instrument and worker confirmation are not retained
events.durability_followup: Continued work, recurrence, trust, and household recovery are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: A case-level individual monetary remedy and employer control response are reported
events.protected_outcome: Reported back pay may compensate part of assessed loss; restored job opportunity and durable security are not observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Opportunity, time, wages, and possible status or household security during the dispute remain unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The resolution moves a reported monetary amount toward the charging party while leaving opportunity restoration and future compliance uncertain
events.later_outcome: Continued work, comparable employment, recurrence, household recovery, trust, political action, switching, and exit are unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No worker-reported fairness, blame, institutional trust, or identity endpoint is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: IER resolution and employer training are reported; no worker organizing, public action, or later complaint is observed
events.counterexample: Payment can address assessed back pay without recreating the lost job or proving durable correction
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official DOJ IER FY2026 summary; payment is agency-reported and not independently confirmed by a worker receipt, and claimant-level follow-up is absent

arrows.evidence: Five dated FY2026 IER summaries describe charging-party employment, recruitment, transfer, or verification disputes followed by resolutions
arrows.counterexample: The summaries are selected resolutions, not a prevalence sample or complete underlying employment record
arrows.remaining_gap: Full chronology, actor identity, application/shift records, alternatives, and counterfactual opportunity

arrows.evidence: Four summaries report individual payments of $5,600, $16,730, $30,000, and $8,000 across four cases; the fifth reports a $485,000 offer, not payment
arrows.counterexample: An agency-reported payment is not an independently audited receipt, and the offer case must not be pooled with paid cases
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment instrument, date, net amount, worker confirmation, acceptance, and case-specific eligibility

arrows.evidence: The summaries report training, Form I-9/E-Verify policy creation, or an explicit anti-discrimination policy change alongside remedies
arrows.counterexample: A stated training or policy change does not establish implementation, monitoring, recurrence prevention, or worker control
arrows.remaining_gap: Completion records, monitoring, enforcement, recurrence, and comparable-worker outcomes

arrows.to: restored work, household security, trust, action, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public summaries report no accepted reinstatement, later employment, household recovery, trust, political action, switching, or exit endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Back pay can compensate assessed loss while the original job, comparable opportunity, or institutional relationship remains changed
arrows.remaining_gap: Stable claimant linkage, alternative work, accepted/refused reinstatement, receipt, net recovery, later employment, recurrence, trust, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes five separate agency-reported IER resolution summaries. It strengthens the individual-remedy stage, but it does not establish worker-confirmed receipt, restored opportunity, durable compliance, household recovery, trust, political action, switching, or exit, and it is not a prevalence estimate.
storage_boundary: No claimant files, direct identifiers, employer identities beyond the public summary boundary, or bulk archive are retained; only bounded case summaries, dates, reported remedy amounts/offers, uncertainty, and open arrows are represented.
